findings.title: retryCount delete condition is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The deleteMany OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the other branch. Any WorkflowReminder row of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount exceeds 1 will be deleted by this SMS cron job. Even though today only this file increments retryCount, the column is shared by all methods (WhatsApp reminders are handled by a separate cron, and the same retry pattern is likely to be reused there), so an email or WhatsApp reminder that failed twice would be silently destroyed by the SMS cron, dropping reminders that other schedulers still need. The retryCount condition should be ANDed with `method: SMS` (and probably `scheduled: false`).

findings.title: retryCount incremented from stale in-memory value instead of atomic increment
findings.body: The update writes `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read at query time. If two cron invocations overlap (or the handler is retried), both read the same retryCount and both write the same incremented value, so failures are undercounted and the retry limit is effectively never enforced. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead.

findings.title: Deletion of over-retried reminders happens a run late and deletes scheduled:false rows mid-cycle
findings.body: Deletion of reminders with retryCount > 1 happens only at the start of the next cron run. A reminder that failed twice (retryCount = 2) is still picked up and scheduled again in the current run (the findMany does not filter retryCount), so it can actually be attempted 3 times, and the Twilio call happens before the deleteMany of the next run removes it. If the intent is 'delete after failing twice', the findMany should exclude retryCount >= 2, or the delete filter timing should be documented/adjusted. This also means a reminder that succeeds on the third attempt is then deleted by the next run's deleteMany (retryCount 2 > 1), discarding the referenceId needed to cancel the scheduled SMS.
